title: Runbook
description: A cached, replayable procedure. Produced by hand (M1) or distilled from a winning trajectory (M3), and executed by the runbook executor (TON-10). This file is the contract between Track A and Track B - locked at H+1, not renegotiated mid-build.

id.description: Stable identifier. Synthesized runbooks append a short suffix to avoid collisions.

source.description: Where this came from. The executor MUST NOT branch on this - if it needs to, TON-21 emitted something wrong.

description.description: What this runbook does, in one sentence. This is what the semantic matcher (TON-15) searches against, so it must describe the TASK, not the implementation.

utterance_examples.description: Phrasings that should match this runbook. Helps the matcher and doubles as the rehearsal script's source of truth.

slots.description: Values the caller must supply. The dialogue layer (TON-9) asks for missing ones in declaration order.

prompt.description: Spoken aloud when this slot is unfilled. Write it as a question a person would actually ask.

steps.description: Executed in order. Stop on first failure - no retries, no recovery.

kind.description: shell runs in the Sailbox; browser drives the persistent profile inside it.

description.description: One line, plain language. Logged, and read aloud on failure.

irreversible.description: INVARIANT 1. True for anything with an out-of-box side effect: bookings, charges, sent messages. The executor MUST route these through the spoken confirm gate, and branches MUST NOT run them.

confirm.description: Spoken readback before an irreversible step. Required when irreversible is true. Must name the specifics (what, when, how much) - 'shall I proceed?' is not acceptable. Supports {{slot}} and {{capture}} templating.

capture.description: Store this step's output under this name, usable as {{name}} in later steps. This is how a price read from the page reaches the confirm line.

command.description: shell only. Runs via /bin/sh -lc. Supports {{...}} templating.

expect.description: Optional success assertion. For browser steps, a selector that must be present after the op. Absence means the step failed.

then.$comment: An irreversible step without a spoken readback is how you book four cars.
